title: llama.cpp: LLMs on Your CPU
description: llama.cpp (by Georgi Gerganov) runs large language model inference in plain C/C++ with zero heavy dependencies — no Python, no CUDA required — on CPUs, and optionally GPUs. It made 7B-70B models runnable on laptops and edge boxes. The tactical AI runtime for disconnected hardware.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: ggml: The Tensor Library
description: ggml is the tensor library underneath llama.cpp — 16-bit floats, integer quantization, and SIMD/GPU backends in compact C. It does for edge inference what BLAS did for servers: the fast math everyone builds on. whisper.cpp and others reuse it.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Quantization: Q4_K_M and Friends
description: Quantization shrinks model weights from 16-bit floats to 4-8 bit integers — Q4_K_M is the beloved balance — cutting a 7B model from 14GB to ~4GB with small quality loss. K-quants group weights for better accuracy per bit. Quantization is what makes big models fit small machines.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: CPU Backends: AVX, NEON, Accelerate
description: llama.cpp compiles SIMD paths for x86 (AVX2/AVX-512), ARM (NEON), and Apple Accelerate — the same model runs fast on a server, a phone chip, or a Mac. Backend selection is automatic at build or runtime. Portable speed.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: GPU Offload: Partial Acceleration
description: llama.cpp offloads layers to GPU — CUDA, Metal, ROCm, Vulkan — keeping the rest on CPU when VRAM is short. n_gpu_layers tunes the split. Partial offload is the pragmatic middle between CPU-only and full-GPU.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Memory Bandwidth Is the Limit
description: LLM inference is memory-bandwidth bound: each token streams the whole model through the processor, so tokens/sec ≈ bandwidth / model size. Faster RAM beats more cores for inference. Sizing edge inference starts with the memory bus.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: GGUF: The Model File Format
description: GGUF is llama.cpp's model file format — metadata plus quantized tensors in one file, replacing the older GGML format. Converters quantize Hugging Face models into GGUF. One file, every backend, everywhere.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Prompt Processing vs Generation
description: Inference has two phases: prompt processing (parallel, fast — the model reads your prompt) and token generation (serial, slow — one token at a time). Long prompts cost upfront; long answers cost per token. Benchmarks quote both: pp tok/s and tg tok/s.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Sampling: Temperature and Top-p
description: Sampling turns logits into tokens: temperature flattens or sharpens the distribution, top-p (nucleus) cuts the tail, repeat penalties fight loops. Tactical deployments tune sampling per task — low temp for extraction, higher for drafting. Decoding is a policy choice.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Server Mode: OpenAI-Compatible API
description: llama.cpp's server mode exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API — existing tools talk to the edge model unchanged. Local inference, standard interface. The edge slots into existing software.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Constrained Grammars (GBNF)
description: GBNF grammars constrain generation to valid JSON, enums, or DSLs — the model cannot emit malformed output. Tactical pipelines need machine-parseable answers, not prose. Grammar is the contract between model and code.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Speculative Decoding
description: Speculative decoding drafts tokens with a small model and verifies with the big one — accepting most drafts, keeping quality, gaining speed. Two models collaborating beat one model waiting. llama.cpp implements it for the speed-hungry.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Benchmarking Edge Inference
description: Edge inference benchmarks report pp/tg tok/s per model, quant, backend, and device — the matrix that sizes deployments. Reproduce before trusting: same flags, same prompt. Numbers without methodology are anecdotes.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Model Provenance and Licensing
description: Edge deployments track model provenance — base model, quantizer, license — because weights carry licenses and some forbid commercial use. The GGUF metadata records the chain. Compliance rides with the file.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Disconnected AI Picture
description: Ladder-top llama.cpp: quantized models, CPU/GPU backends, local server API, grammars for structure, benchmarks for sizing. Fifteen rungs from C code to capable AI on hardware with no internet at all.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
